label: MODEL_DERIVED — manufacturing process based on public medical-device industry standards; not validated with actual vendor quotes
question: Could a competent medical-device engineering team actually build this prototype?
answer: YES — with caveats. All materials are FDA-cleared for vascular/CNS implant. All processes are standard medical-device manufacturing. Novel integration is the membrane-sleeve bonding step.

material_specification.shunt_body: Pebax 6333 SA01 MED (Arkema) — standard catheter material
material_specification.membrane: ePTFE, 0.05um pore, 50um thick (W.L. Gore or Zeus)
material_specification.bypass_valve: Titanium spring (ASTM F67) + silicone valve seat (Nusil MED-4750)

procurement_form.Pebax: Extruded tubing, 0.5mm ID × 0.8mm OD, cut to 80mm length

membrane_fabrication_method: Purchase ePTFE sheet from Gore/Zeus; laser cut to sleeve geometry; no in-house fabrication needed
integration_process: Step 1: Cut Pebax tubing to 80mm length
Step 2: Laser drill bypass port at midpoint
Step 3: Insert titanium spring + silicone valve seat into bypass port
Step 4: Wrap ePTFE membrane sleeve around inner lumen at membrane zone
Step 5: Bond membrane edges with medical-grade epoxy (UV cure)
Step 6: Attach tantalum radiopaque markers at proximal and distal ends
Step 7: Final inspection (leak test, flow test)
bonding_attachment_process: UV-cured medical epoxy; bond strength validated per ASTM D1002
sterilization: EtO (standard for polymer implants); gamma not recommended (degrades ePTFE)
inspection: Statistical sampling for membrane bond strength (ASTM D1002)
accelerated_aging: ASTM F1980 — 5-year simulated aging at 55°C; validate membrane integrity and spring force
chronic_degradation_risks: ePTFE creep under chronic pressure load
Epoxy bond degradation in CSF environment
